clue.text: Short note Stateside lawyer returned promptly for example

indicators.note: returned says the two pieces together are read backwards
short says the note loses its final letter

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A brief memo from an American attorney came back quickly, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: A breve is a note worth two semibreves; 'Short' docks its E, and 'returned' turns the whole BREVDA round. 'promptly' is not the definition alone: it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Promptly is a word modifying a verb, an example of that part of speech.

clue.text: Slow down in river when treacle stirred in?

indicators.note: in says the stirred letters go inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales and England and in Scotland

indicators.note: stirred says the letters of treacle are mixed up

explanation.surface: Does treacle stirred into a river slow it down?
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' makes CELERAT from the syrup; the Dee is a favourite crossword river. The surface's sticky logic, treacle slowing the flow, makes it nearly an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: To decelerate is to reduce speed.

clue.text: Language Beardsley uses occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally says only every other letter of the name is used

explanation.surface: The artist Aubrey Beardsley sometimes drops a word of a certain tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Composer able to play with another? Fair enough

indicators.note: to play says the letters of able are toyed with and rearranged

parts.note: Lionel Bart, composer of the musical Oliver!, is another composer
OK is said to accept something as fair enough

explanation.surface: A composer who can perform alongside someone else: reasonable enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another composer, Lionel Bart, besides the one defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Bela Bartok was a Hungarian composer of the 20th century.

clue.text: Traveller with hat and moccasin perhaps

parts.note: a rep is a travelling salesperson
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A wayfarer wearing a hat and soft leather shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moccasin' is not the shoe: the water moccasin is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The water moccasin is a venomous American snake, an example of a reptile.

clue.text: Irish giving support to saint excited reaction

indicators.note: giving support to says the Irish letters sit beneath the saint in the down entry

explanation.surface: An Irishman backing a saint provokes a strong response.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or flurry of public excitement.

clue.text: Opera singer, new in Norma, paid badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters are put in a poor order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A soprano in a new production of Bellini's Norma gets a poor fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is the leading female singer in an opera company.

clue.text: Hawk-headed god restrained outside produces trumpet

indicators.note: outside says the restrained word wraps round the god

parts.note: held means restrained
Ra, the Egyptian sun god, is shown with a hawk's head

explanation.surface: An Egyptian god held in check yields a fanfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trumpet' is a verb here, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald something is to announce or proclaim it loudly, as trumpeting it does.

clue.text: Academic worried by Burke or Hare finally choosing body

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter, and Burke and Hare both end in the same one

parts.note: a lector is a university lecturer
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

explanation.surface: A scholar fretting over the infamous body-snatchers Burke and Hare.
explanation.walkthrough: Burke and Hare were 19th-century Edinburgh murderers who sold corpses for dissection; both names end in E, so 'or' does no harm.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole set of voters, the group that chooses representatives.

clue.text: Supporter brings complaint about northern player

indicators.note: about says the complaint word goes round the northern letter

parts.note: a beef is a grievance or complaint
an actor plays parts on stage

explanation.surface: A backer lodges a grievance about a performer from the North.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor gives money or help, so is a patron and backer.

clue.text: Yucatan native is allowed to answer

parts.note: may means is permitted to

explanation.surface: A local of Mexico's Yucatan gets permission to reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maya are the indigenous people whose civilisation centred on the Yucatan peninsula.

clue.text: Fierce chap avoiding pained expression

indicators.note: avoiding says the cry of pain is left out of the chap word

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
ow is what someone says when hurt

explanation.surface: A ferocious man who never lets on that something hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expression' suggests a face, but here it is a spoken cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell is a literary adjective for cruel or savage, as in 'one fell swoop'.

clue.text: Creep around behind seven others, hiding head in tower

indicators.note: around says the creep word goes round the trimmed ordinal

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person, a creep

indicators.note: hiding head says the ordinal loses its first letter

parts.note: coming behind seven others places you eighth

explanation.surface: Someone sneaking past seven people to hide their face inside a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind seven others' is a position in a queue, eighth; 'hiding head' drops its first letter, leaving IGHTH. 'Creep' is a noun, a louse.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighthouse is a tower with a beacon to guide ships.

clue.text: Island retreats predicted to keep one healthy

indicators.note: retreats says the island's name goes backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

indicators.note: to keep says the predicted word holds one inside

parts.note: boded means foretold or predicted
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Island getaways promised to keep a person fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' looks like a noun for holiday spots but is a verb turning the island back. Elba is where Napoleon was first exiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Able-bodied means physically fit and strong, free of disability.

clue.text: Fought over Scandinavian money racket

indicators.note: over places the fought word above the money in the down entry

parts.note: battled means fought
the ore is a coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Clashed about Nordic cash in some swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests a scam, but it is the bat used in the old game.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore is the wooden bat used in battledore and shuttlecock, forerunner of badminton.

clue.text: Digital TV one cleric ordered, lacking in volume

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are put into a new order
lacking in says the volume letter is missing from the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A digital television set one priest bought, with the sound off.
explanation.walkthrough: TV ONE CLERIC with V taken out leaves letters 'ordered' into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic and digital both describe technology based on circuitry and computers.

clue.text: China to annex central region in large coastal town

indicators.note: to annex says the friend takes the middle letters inside

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate)

indicators.note: central region picks out the inner letters of the word large

explanation.surface: China seizing the heartland of a big seaside town reads like geopolitics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: rhyming slang 'china plate' is mate. MARGATE is a seaside resort in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is a resort town on the Kent coast of England.

clue.text: Peach stone brought to athlete missing start

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

indicators.note: missing start says the athlete word loses its first letter

parts.note: a runner is an athlete

explanation.surface: A fruit stone handed to a sprinter who missed the starting gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peach' and 'stone' suggest fruit, but peach means a beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is informally a very attractive person, as is a stunner.

clue.text: Check on heartbeat

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a pulse is a heartbeat

explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to check or drive it back.

clue.text: Poor Kathleen stops totally heartless devil passing on ring

indicators.note: stops says the shuffled name plugs the gap in the outer letters
totally heartless keeps only the first and last letters of the word devil
poor says the letters of the name are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Unlucky Kathleen halts a soulless demon by handing on a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges the name to EATHKNEL; 'totally heartless' strips every inner letter of devil, not just the centre one, leaving DL.
explanation.definitionFit: A death knell is a bell tolled to announce a death, someone passing on.

clue.text: Be sent north in time for discussion

indicators.note: in says the reversed piece goes inside the time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: sent north says the word be goes upwards in the down entry, so reads backwards

explanation.surface: Be sent up north at some point for talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal discussion of opposing views.

clue.text: Page cut from agreements in book before Romans

indicators.note: cut from says the page letter is removed from the agreements word

parts.note: pacts are agreements

explanation.surface: A page removed from treaties in a volume preceding a Roman history.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is the New Testament book immediately preceding the Epistle to the Romans.

clue.text: Energy from cheese endlessly served with egg?

indicators.note: endlessly says the cheese loses its final letter

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese
an egg is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Where vigour comes from: cheese served up with an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is liveliness and vigour, as in playing music with brio.

clue.text: Slap bottom?

definitions.meaning: slap is British theatrical slang for makeup
the bottom or base of a building

explanation.surface: Smack someone's backside?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a spanking, but both words are nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Foundation is base makeup (slap) and also the lowest load-bearing part of a structure.

clue.text: Skin taken from disloyal follower in uprising

indicators.note: in uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
taken from says the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Flesh removed from a treacherous henchman in a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft made 'Skin taken' the definition and left 'from' with no job; 'taken from' is the hiding signal and 'Skin' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay is to strip the skin off, so skin as a verb.

clue.text: Son leaving belt in corner

indicators.note: leaving says the son letter departs from the belt word

parts.note: a strap is a belt

explanation.surface: A boy abandoning his belt in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corner' is a verb: to trap someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To corner a person is to trap them with no way out.

clue.text: Intruder right to chase second ball lodged in tree

indicators.note: to chase says the right letter follows behind
lodged in says the second and ball pieces sit inside the tree

parts.note: taken as written
a ball in football is a pass to a teammate

explanation.surface: An intruder retrieving a ball stuck up a tree, rightly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespasser enters land without permission, an unwelcome intruder.

clue.text: Lover no longer kissed we hear — imagine!

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: we hear says the next word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: pecked means gave a quick kiss

explanation.surface: An old flame gave someone a quick kiss, the gossip says: just imagine!
explanation.definitionFit: 'I expect' means 'I suppose', so expect can mean imagine or presume.
